text:
maria (infra): heads up — starting ~10m ago we saw leader flips in etcd and controller-manager OOM/crashloop in us-east1-gpu-02. GPU node pool autoscaler fenced a subset of the zone. pods in gpu-pool-* are stuck Terminating, new allocs failing. :rotating_light:
jin (sre): ugh. any specific error in apiserver logs?
maria (infra): apiserver shows `conn reset by peer` and `failed to write response: write tcp` around leader flip times. etcd logs show slow disk > 200ms for raft append, and follower catchups timing out.
ash (typo) nate (platform): hitting SNAT exhaustion earlier today in that region? I remember a NAT issue this morning.
jin (sre): checking NAT counters — looks like ephemeral SNATs at 95% for that subnet, could explain proxy timeouts.
ash (mistake) maria (infra): also saw the cloud provider mark 3 hosts as maintenance which triggered pod evacuation. Autoscaler fence policy nuked the schedulable capacity and we hit quorum stress.
ash corrected: nate (platform): copying logs: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=controller-manager -o wide` shows controller-manager crashed on 3 replicas.
ash (typo) ashley (oncall): ops-bot created incident INC-2024-198 with low threshold, paging team.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-198 created: Control plane instability in us-east1-gpu-02. Severity: P2. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/controlplane-quorum.json
maria (infra): temporary mitigation idea: cordon the fenced nodes, scale up a cross-zone standby GPU pool in us-east1-b to pick up workloads, and promote an etcd snapshot leader from healthy nodes.
jin (sre): agree. I'm promoting a snapshot to force compact and reduce follower catch-up backlog. running: `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /var/lib/etcd/member/snap/db` and `etcdctl defrag`.
nash (nate): I'll open a cloud support ticket and ask to cancel the maintenance on those hosts. Also increasing SNAT pool size to avoid proxy resets.
ash (typo) ashley (oncall): quick fix: scale controller-manager replicas to 5 temporarily so leader election can succeed despite restarts.
jin (sre): applied `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment controller-manager --replicas=5` — watching rollouts. logs show fewer crash loops now.
maria (infra): discovered kube-proxy was OOM'ing on the fenced nodes due to iptables churn from heavy ephemeral port usage. Might be partly due to aggressive client retry loops from upstream serving runtime.
nate (platform): added a temporary iptables conntrack-tuning snippet to cloud-init for new nodes; also bumped kube-proxy memory request. link: `https://redwood.internal/ops/conntrack-tuning.md`
jin (sre): after defrag and promoting snapshot leader, etcd RTTs dropped to ~20ms, followers started catching up. controller-manager stabilized.
maria (infra): pods stuck Terminating — ran `kubectl patch pod <pod> -n ml-apps -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'` for a few blocked ones, that freed up allocations.
nash (nate): cost note: the cross-zone standby and extra controller-manager replicas will add a small hourly cost bump. I'll quantify and post numbers to #finance later.
ash (typo) ashley (oncall): ops-bot closing incident once metrics stable for 15m.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-198 status: monitoring -> resolved (15m stable). :white_check_mark:
maria (infra): follow-ups: 1) increase SNAT pool for us-east1-gpu-02, 2) add conntrack tuning to node bootstrap, 3) revisit autoscaler fencing thresholds (too aggressive), 4) add an on-call run to test leader promotion steps during maintenance.
jin (sre): filing a GH issue in infra/etcd with logs and config diffs.
nate (platform): I'll post the cost impact and a rollback plan for standby pool.
maria (infra): thanks everyone. we should write a short postmortem with timeline and next actions. :thumbsup:
